chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, caused Adam and his wife to eat of the wheat, He expelled them both from Paradise and caused them to descend to the earth. Adam descended upon al-Safa and Hawwa descended upon al-Marwa. Al-Safa was named thus because it was derived from the name of Adam al-Mustafa (the Chosen), corresponding to the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely Allah chose Adam and Noah.' And al-Marwa was named Marwa because it was derived from the name al-Mar'a (the woman).

Adam said: 'Nothing separated me from her except that she is not permissible for me. Had she been permissible for me, she would have descended with me upon al-Safa, but she was forbidden to me because of that, and separation was effected between me and her.'

Adam remained isolated from Hawwa. He would visit her during the day, conversing with her upon al-Marwa. But when night came and he feared being overcome by his desires, he would return to al-Safa and sleep there. Adam had no comfort except her, and for that reason women were called 'nisa'', because Hawwa was the 'uns' (companionship/comfort) for Adam.

Allah neither spoke to him nor sent him a messenger. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed upon him repentance and conveyed to him certain words. When he spoke these words, Allah turned towards him in mercy and sent Jibraeel (peace be upon him) to him. He said: 'Peace be upon you, O Adam, you who repent from your error and are patient through your tribulation. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent me to you to teach you the rites through which you can be purified.'

He took him by his hand and led him to the place of the House (Ka'ba). Allah sent down upon him a cloud that shaded the place of the House, and the cloud was aligned with the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the Frequented House above). He said: 'O Adam, mark with your foot the area where this cloud has shaded you, for a house of white gem will be brought forth for you, becoming your qibla and the qibla of your offspring after you.' Adam (peace be upon him) did so, and Allah brought forth beneath the cloud a house of white gem. And Allah sent down the Black Stone, which was whiter than milk and more radiant than the sun; it turned black only because the polytheists wiped themselves with it — from the filth of the polytheists the Stone turned black. Jibraeel (peace be upon him) commanded him to seek Allah's forgiveness from his sin at all the sacred sites, and informed him that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had forgiven him, and instructed him to carry pebbles for the jamarat from al-Muzdalifa.

When he reached the place of the jamarat, Iblees confronted him and said: 'O Adam, where are you headed?' Jibraeel (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do not speak to him; pelt him with seven pebbles and proclaim the takbir with each pebble.' So Adam (peace be upon him) did so until he had finished pelting the stones.

He commanded him to offer the sacrifice — that is, the hady (sacrificial animal) — before pelting the jamarat. And he commanded him to shave his head in humility before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So Adam did that. Then he commanded him to visit the House and circumambulate it seven times, and to hasten between al-Safa and al-Marwa seven times, beginning at al-Safa and ending at al-Marwa.

Then he commanded him to visit the House, to circumambulate it seven times, and to walk briskly between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa seven times, beginning at Al-Safa and ending at Al-Marwa. Then after that, he circumambulated seven more times around the House — this is the Tawaf al-Nisa'. It is not permissible for the one in ihram to approach his wife until he performs the Tawaf al-Nisa'. Adam (peace be upon him) did so.

Then Jibraeel said to him: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forgiven your sin, accepted your repentance, and made your wife permissible to you.' So Adam went forth, and his sin was forgiven, his repentance was accepted, and his wife was made permissible to him.

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Safa and al-Marwa — the two hills in Mecca between which sa'y is performed
key_terms.الْبَيْتُ الْمَعْمُورُ: Bayt al-Ma'mur — the Frequented House in the heavens, the celestial counterpart to the Ka'ba
key_terms.الْجِمَارُ: The jamarat — the stone pillars representing Iblees, pelted during hajj
key_terms.الْحَجَرُ الْأَسْوَدُ: The Black Stone — originally white, turned black from polytheists' contact
key_terms.الْحِنْطَةَ: The wheat — the forbidden fruit Adam and Hawwa ate in Paradise
key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكُ: The hajj rites/rituals taught by Jibraeel to Adam
key_terms.الْمَهَاة: White gem (onyx/crystal) — the material from which the first Ka'ba was built
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَةُ: Muzdalifa — the sacred plain where hajj pilgrims spend the night and collect pebbles
key_terms.الْمُصْطَفَى: Al-Mustafa — the Chosen One, an epithet of Adam (and later the Prophet Muhammad)
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-nisa' — the circumambulation that makes one's spouse permissible again after ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the hajj rituals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), narrating through Imam al-Kadhim (peace be upon him), recounts the origin narrative of hajj: after Adam and Hawwa were expelled from Paradise for eating the wheat, they descended separately — Adam on al-Safa and Hawwa on al-Marwa — and remained separated during a period of divine silence. The Imam explains the etymological origins of the names 'Safa' (from al-Mustafa, the Chosen) and 'Marwa' (from al-Mar'a, the woman), and 'nisa'' (women, from 'uns', companionship). Upon Adam's repentance, Angel Jibraeel taught him the complete hajj rituals — including tawaf, sa'y, the Ka'ba's establishment, the Black Stone's descent, stoning of Iblees at the jamarat, sacrifice, shaving, and tawaf al-nisa' — by which his sin was expiated and his wife was restored to him. This narrative provides the theological foundation for hajj as an act of purification, rooted in Adam's original sin and repentance.

Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Husayn Bin Yazeed, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, when Adamas and hisas wife attained from the wheat, Exited both of themas from the Paradise, and Caused them to descend to the earth. So Adamas descended upon Al-Safaas, and Hawwaas descended upon Al-Marwa, and rather, Al-Safa was named as ‘Safa; because it was derived for himas, from the name of Adamas, the chosen one (Al-Mustafa), and that is due to the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [3:33] Surely Allah Chose Adam and Noah. And Al-Marwa was named ‘Marwa’ because it was derived for heras, from the name ‘Al-Mar’a’ (The woman).

So Adam<sup>as</sup> said: ‘There would not have been a separation between me<sup>as</sup> and her<sup>as</sup>, except that she is not Permissible unto me<sup>as</sup>, and had she<sup>as</sup> been Permissible unto me<sup>as</sup>, she<sup>as</sup> would have descended with me<sup>as</sup> upon Al-Safa, but she<sup>as</sup> is Forbidden unto me<sup>as</sup> due to the reason of that, and separation has been effected between me<sup>as</sup> and her<sup>as</sup>’.

Thus, Adam<sup>as</sup> remained isolated from Hawwa<sup>as</sup>. So he<sup>as</sup> used to go to her at daytime, discussing with her<sup>as</sup> upon Al-Marwa. So whenever it was the night, and he<sup>as</sup> feared of being overcome by his<sup>as</sup> self (desire), would return to Al-Safa, and he<sup>as</sup> would sleep upon it. And, Adam<sup>as</sup> did not have a comfort  apart from her<sup>as</sup>, and due to that, the woman (Al-Nisa) has been named as such, as Hawwa<sup>as</sup> was the ‘Ansa’ (comfort) for Adam<sup>as</sup>.

Neither did Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Spoke to him<sup>as</sup>, nor did He<sup>azwj</sup> Send a Messenger to him<sup>as</sup>. Then, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Favoured upon him<sup>as</sup> with the repentance, and Dictated him<sup>as</sup> certain words. So when he<sup>as</sup> spoke by these, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Turned towards him<sup>as</sup> (with Mercy) and Sent Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> unto him<sup>as</sup>’. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Greeting be unto you<sup>as</sup>, O Adam<sup>as</sup>, the repentant one from his<sup>as</sup> error, the patient upon his<sup>as</sup> tribulation. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent me<sup>as</sup> to you<sup>as</sup>, to teach you<sup>as</sup> the rituals through which you<sup>as</sup> can be purified.

So he<sup>as</sup> grabbed his<sup>as</sup> hand and went with him<sup>as</sup> to the place of the House (Kaaba), and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent down the cloud upon him<sup>as</sup>. So it shaded the place of the House, and the cloud used to be by the side of the Bayt Al-Ma’mour (The oft-frequented House). So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Adam<sup>as</sup>! Mark with your<sup>as</sup> foot where this cloud has shaded upon you<sup>as</sup>, for a house of white gem would be extracted for you, becoming your<sup>as</sup> Qiblah (direction), and a Qiblah of your<sup>as</sup> offspring from after you<sup>as</sup>’.
So Adam<sup>as</sup> did so, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Brought out a House of white gem for him<sup>as</sup> beneath the cloud, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent down the Black Stone, and it used to be intensely whiter than the milk, and more illuminating than the sun. But rather, it turned black because the Polytheists used to wipe with it, thus it is from the filth of the Polytheists, the Stone turned black. And, Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> instructed him<sup>as</sup> that he<sup>as</sup> should seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from his<sup>as</sup> sins at the entirety of the Signs, and informed him<sup>as</sup> that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic had Forgiven him<sup>asws</sup>, and instructed him<sup>as</sup> to carry a number of pebbles of stones from Al-Muzdalifa.

So when heas reached the place of the pebbles, Ibleesla appeared to himas, and hela said to himas, ‘O Adamla! Where are youasws intending (to go to)?’ So Jibraeelas said to himas: ‘Do not speak to himla, and pelt himas with seven pebbles, and exclaim Takbeer with each pebble’. So Adamas did it, until heas was free from pelting the stones.

And he<sup>as</sup> instructed him<sup>as</sup> that he<sup>as</sup> should offer the sacrifice, and it is the sacrificial animal, before the pelting of the stones. And he<sup>as</sup> instructed him<sup>as</sup> that he<sup>as</sup> should shave his<sup>as</sup> head, in reverence to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. So Adam<sup>as</sup> did that.

Then he<sup>as</sup> instructed him<sup>as</sup> with the visitation of the House (Kaaba), and that he<sup>as</sup> should circumambulate with it seven (times), and he<sup>as</sup> should walk briskly between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, seven (times), beginning with Al-Safa and ending at Al-Marwa.

Then, after that, heas circumambulated seven (times) by the House (Kaaba), and it is the circumambulation of the wife (Tawaaf Al-Nisa), it not being Permissible for the one in Ihraam that he should approach his wife until he has done the Tawaaf Al-Nisa. So Adamas did so.  So Jibraeelas said to himas: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Forgiven youras sins, and Accepted youras repentance, and Permitted youras wife for youas’. So Adamas went, and hisas sins were Forgiven for himas, and hisas repentance having been Accepted from himas, and hisas wife having been Permitted unto himas’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from al-Husayn ibn Yazid from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “Abu Ibrahim from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, when Adam and his spouse were affected by the tree of wheat, expelled them from paradise and made them to descend to earth. Adam landed on al-Safa’ and Hawwa’ (Eve) landed on al- Marwah. Al-Safa’ is called by this name because it is derived from Adam’s name al-Mustafa’ (the chosen one) as Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has said, “Allah chose Adam and Noah.” [3:33] Al-Marwah is called by this name because it is taken from the word al-Mar’ah (a woman).
Adam then said to himself, “Allah has separated her from me is because she is not lawful for me anymore; had she been lawful for me she would descend with me on al-Safa’.”

Adam waited away from Hawwa’. He would go to her at al-Marwah during the day and speak to her. At night, for fear that his desires may overcome him, would go back to al-Safa’ and pass the night there. Adam had no one beside Hawwa’ to comfort him and for this reason women are called al-Nisa’ (comforting). Hawwa’ was a source of comfort for Adam.

Allah did not speak to him and did not send any messenger to him. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, then accepted his repentance as a favor to him. He dictated to him certain words. Adam then spoke those words and Allah turned to him with the acceptance of his repentance. He then sent Jibril to him, who offered him the greeting of peace and said, “O repenting Adam, who has turned back from his mistakes and exercised patience on facing misfortune. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has sent me to you to teach the good deeds which when you practice will cleanse you.”

He then took hold of his hand and moved to the site of the House. Allah sent a piece of cloud and it cast a shadow on the site of the House. The cloud was parallel to the established House in the heaven. Jibril said, “O Adam, draw a mark with your foot around the shadow of this cloud, that has covered the site. A house of diamond will soon emerge for you on this site, which will be a Qiblah for you and your descendants after you.” Adam did as he was told to do and Allah then made a house of diamond emerge for him under the cloud. Allah brought down the Black Stone, which at that time was intensely white, even more than milk and brighter than the sun. It turned black because of the pagans’ touch and because of their filth. Jibril commanded Adam to ask forgiveness from Allah for his sin, near all the reminders (of Allah) and would tell him that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has forgiven him. He commanded him to pick up pebbles, to throw on al-Jamar, from al-Muzdalifah (name of a place).

When he arrived at the place of al-Jamar, Satan countered him and said, “O Adam, where are you going?” Jibril told Adam not to speak to him, pelt him with seven pebbles and say Takhir (Allah is great beyond description) with each throw. Adam did as he was told to do until he completed throwing pebbles on al-Jamar.

He then commanded him to offer a sacrifice, the offering, which is done before throwing pebbles. He commanded him to shave his head to express humbleness before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious. Adam did as he was told to do.

He (Jibril) then commanded him to visit the House, walk seven times around it and walk seven times between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah, beginning from al-Safa’ to end at al-Marwah. Thereafter walk seven times around the House, which is called Tawaf of women. Without this Tawaf, carnal relation remains unlawful. Adam completed this Tawaf

and Jibril said to him, “Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has forgiven your sin, accepted your repentance and your returning to Him. He has made your spouse lawful for you.” Adam then left, his sin was forgiven, his return to Allah was accepted and his spouse became lawful for him.’”
